cards.title: Progress is not the headline
cards.question: You spent 48 hours isolating a PCIe loss issue. What belongs in your first sentence?
cards.selfCheck: Lead with the system risk or decision: channel margin or layout release may be affected. Then give evidence and next checkpoint.
cards.prompt: Explain risk-first hardware engineering updates with a 30-second script and realistic PCIe example.

cards.title: Thirty seconds. No rabbit hole.
cards.question: Your manager asks: What changed, why care, and what do you need?
cards.selfCheck: Use new evidence → system consequence → next proof point → owner or decision request. Label uncertainty.
cards.prompt: Give a Principal Engineer communication drill for a hardware SI/PI debug.

cards.title: State your leading hypothesis
cards.question: How do you communicate an unresolved via-transition problem without sounding uncertain or overconfident?
cards.selfCheck: Say: Via transition is the leading hypothesis; we are comparing EM extraction and TDR to confirm. Give the next decision date.
cards.prompt: Teach calibrated confidence language in SI/PI engineering with examples.

cards.title: Why did nobody know?
cards.question: When should you flag a possible schedule or margin risk?
cards.selfCheck: Communicate early, before root cause is proven, when a decision could be affected. Separate observed facts, likelihood, and next proof.
cards.prompt: Teach proactive engineering risk communication with a 2-minute exercise.
